new_for_interval.brief: Creates a new `GtkLevelBar` for the specified interval.
new_for_interval.md: Creates a new `GtkLevelBar` for the specified interval.

add_offset_value.brief: Adds a new offset marker on `self` at the position specified by `value`.
add_offset_value.md:
Adds a new offset marker on `self` at the position specified by `value`.

When the bar value is in the interval topped by `value` (or between `value`
and [`LevelBar:max-value`](xref:gtk:Gtk.LevelBar#property:max-value) in case the offset is the last one
on the bar) a style class named `level-`@name will be applied
when rendering the level bar fill.

If another offset marker named `name` exists, its value will be
replaced by `value`.

get_inverted.brief: Returns whether the levelbar is inverted.
get_inverted.md: Returns whether the levelbar is inverted.

get_offset_value.brief: Fetches the value specified for the offset marker `name` in `self`.
get_offset_value.md: Fetches the value specified for the offset marker `name` in `self`.

remove_offset_value.brief: Removes an offset marker from a `GtkLevelBar`.
remove_offset_value.md:
Removes an offset marker from a `GtkLevelBar`.

The marker must have been previously added with
[`LevelBar.add_offset_value()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.LevelBar#method:add_offset_value).

set_max_value.md:
Sets the `max-value` of the `GtkLevelBar`.

You probably want to update preexisting level offsets after calling
this function.

set_min_value.md:
Sets the `min-value` of the `GtkLevelBar`.

You probably want to update preexisting level offsets after calling
this function.

inverted.md:
Whether the `GtkLeveBar` is inverted.

Level bars normally grow from top to bottom or left to right.
Inverted level bars grow in the opposite direction.

max-value.brief: Determines the maximum value of the interval that can be displayed by the bar.
max-value.md: Determines the maximum value of the interval that can be displayed by the bar.

min-value.brief: Determines the minimum value of the interval that can be displayed by the bar.
min-value.md: Determines the minimum value of the interval that can be displayed by the bar.

mode.brief: Determines the way `GtkLevelBar` interprets the value properties to draw the level fill area.
mode.md:
Determines the way `GtkLevelBar` interprets the value properties to draw the
level fill area.

Specifically, when the value is %GTK_LEVEL_BAR_MODE_CONTINUOUS,
`GtkLevelBar` will draw a single block representing the current value in
that area; when the value is %GTK_LEVEL_BAR_MODE_DISCRETE,
the widget will draw a succession of separate blocks filling the
draw area, with the number of blocks being equal to the units separating
the integral roundings of [`LevelBar:min-value`](xref:gtk:Gtk.LevelBar#property:min-value) and
[`LevelBar:max-value`](xref:gtk:Gtk.LevelBar#property:max-value).

value.brief: Determines the currently filled value of the level bar.
value.md: Determines the currently filled value of the level bar.

offset-changed.brief: Emitted when an offset specified on the bar changes value.
offset-changed.md:
Emitted when an offset specified on the bar changes value.

This typically is the result of a [`LevelBar.add_offset_value()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.LevelBar#method:add_offset_value)
call.

The signal supports detailed connections; you can connect to the
detailed signal "changed::x" in order to only receive callbacks when
the value of offset "x" changes.
